reason: No challenger passes the rule, so linear_co2 stays. linear_cum_emissions: +0.1 pts, wins 2/3 -> fails; linear_co2_regional: -2.9 pts, wins 1/3 -> fails; linear_co2_per_square: -1.8 pts, wins 1/3 -> fails; hybrid_regional_gbm: -7.8 pts, wins 0/3 -> fails
rule: challenger needs average skill > reference + 5 points and wins at least 2 of 3 exams; eligible: ['linear_cum_emissions', 'linear_co2_regional', 'linear_co2_per_square', 'hybrid_regional_gbm']
notes: India yearly values are plain averages over squares, not area-weighted
models predict from same-month CO2 and past El Nino; scenarios use chosen CO2 paths

descriptions.baseline_zero: Baseline. Predicts every month is normal (anomaly 0). The skill score measures how much better than this each model is.
descriptions.baseline_own_trend: Baseline. Each square's own straight line over time, fitted on training years and extended forward. Strong, but it cannot answer 'what if CO2 changes', so it cannot be champion.
descriptions.natural_only: Natural factors only: El Nino (previous 1, 3, 6 months and 12-month average), place and season. No CO2. If this misses the warming and the CO2 models catch it, that is our own evidence of the human cause.
descriptions.linear_co2: Natural factors plus CO2 in the air (radiative forcing, 5.35 x ln(CO2/280)). One CO2 effect for all of India. Reference model for the champion rule.
descriptions.linear_cum_emissions: Same as linear_co2 but uses total human CO2 emitted since 1751 (world, GtCO2) instead of CO2 in the air.
descriptions.linear_co2_regional: linear_co2, but the CO2 effect may differ by latitude, longitude and season (smooth map), because some regions and months warm faster.
descriptions.linear_co2_per_square: linear_co2, then each square gets its own extra CO2 sensitivity, learned from its own history.
descriptions.hybrid_regional_gbm: linear_co2_regional first; then gradient boosting (small decision trees) learns the leftover patterns from El Nino, place and season. CO2 stays in the linear part because trees cannot go beyond training CO2 levels.
